    def dfun(self, state_variables, coupling, local_coupling=0):

        # shape (n_sv, n_modes)
        S_e = state_variables[0, :]
        S_i = state_variables[1, :]

        G = self.G
        I_ext = self.I_ext
        I_o = self.I_o
        J_N = self.J_N
        J_i = self.J_i
        W_e = self.W_e

        b_i = self.b_i

        gamma_i = self.gamma_i
        lamda = self.lamda
        tau_e = self.tau_e
        tau_i = self.tau_i
        w_p = self.w_p

        # Coupling Terms (from coupling array)
        c_glob = coupling[0, :]

        # Derived Variables
        self.J_N_S_e = J_N_S_e = J_N * S_e
        self.coupling = coupling = G * J_N * (c_glob + S_e * local_coupling)
        self.x_e = x_e = -b_e + a_e * (
            I_ext + coupling + I_o * W_e + J_N_S_e * w_p - J_i * S_i
        )
        self.x_i = x_i = -b_i + a_i * (J_N_S_e - S_i + I_o * W_i + coupling * lamda)
        self.H_e = H_e = x_e / (1 - np.exp(-d_e * x_e))
        self.H_i = H_i = x_i / (1 - np.exp(-d_i * x_i))

        # Time Derivatives
        # Broadcast every derivative to a common per-node shape so constant
        # (state-independent) derivatives — e.g. ``duA/dt = cA`` — stack into a
        # homogeneous array alongside node-shaped ones, matching TVB's own

            np.asarray(H_i * gamma_i - S_i / tau_i),  # S_i
        )
        return np.array(_derivs)
